title: fix(doctor): carry the recorded failure in session SQLite recovery reports
body:
Fixes #156218. Thanks @s93101179 for the report.

## What Problem This Solves

Session SQLite recovery could generate an empty support issue without explaining the original failure. The later zero-issue guard also hid recorded failures when recovery validated cleanly.

## User Impact

Recovery reports retain the original run ID, target, failure code/error, and recorded failure timestamp alongside the recovery outcome. Empty recovery prints `nothing to recover; no report filed` and generates no issue body. Prepared-transcript changes still reject the import batch; the existing rejection test is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [2026.9.5 recovery owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-recover-report.ts#L103) unconditionally generated a report. The journal already supports target issues and `failedAt`, but importer exceptions escaped before those facts were recorded, and rendering omitted the timestamp.

The [import owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eaf063e627e2d98208e0d2b8e866baee055038a9/src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-import.ts#L69) now records the failure before rethrowing. A journal-write failure retains both causes in an aggregate error. The existing import implementation moves into a focused sibling to satisfy the line-cap gate; the orchestration module shrinks by 196 lines. The [recovery owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eaf063e627e2d98208e0d2b8e866baee055038a9/src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-recover-report.ts#L138) reads those facts and preserves reports for actual restoration or import work; the [renderer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/eaf063e627e2d98208e0d2b8e866baee055038a9/src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-failure.ts#L266) carries the recorded timestamp.

No database/manifest schema, options, dependencies, archive retention, or rollback semantics change. Existing operator journals remain the input; missing historical timestamps say `not recorded`.

The `<!-- openclaw-report:… -->` hash covers the exact generated body. New reports include the timestamp; reports with an existing issue-handoff receipt remain byte-for-byte unchanged for duplicate reconciliation.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m36q7pyfckmky3cntv60s3kc`, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35839243584). All state and data were synthetic and isolated; issue submission used a local print stub.
- Six regression assertions failed against the original implementation. Final focused runs passed all 53 tests, including the unchanged prepared-transcript rejection contract.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <all eight changed paths>` passed: formatting, line-cap and suppression ratchets, core and core-test typechecks, lint, dead exports, import cycles, storage guards, and documentation checks.
- Full cross-lane set: **47 files, 1,346 tests passed, 2 existing platform-specific cases skipped**. All 513 updater cases completed once on the final implementation; the four E2E files passed separately (41 tests, 94.29 s test-run duration).
- `update-cli.test.ts` completed all 513 cases: **283.37 s file wall time**, measured by the native JSON reporter. Its real-process transport fixture is unchanged; fixture performance remains a separate follow-up and does not gate this fix.
- Live CLI: a real rejected SQLite migration exited 2, left the rejected session row absent, and durably recorded its error and timestamp. `doctor --session-sqlite recover --github-issue --yes` carried those exact facts into the captured body. A separate empty recovery emitted the explicit non-outcome and created neither report artifacts nor a submission.
- Independent review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

```text
REJECTED_BATCH_ROW_ABSENT=passed
LIVE_FAILURE_REPORT_ASSERTIONS=passed
session-sqlite recover: nothing to recover; no report filed
LIVE_NOOP_ASSERTIONS=passed
```

Changed test-file costs (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, including shared preparation): `doctor-session-sqlite.failure-reports.test.ts` **33.72 s** / 19 tests; `doctor.test.ts` **18.20 s** / 23 tests. CI job times are pending at author handoff.

The combined JSON reporter could not initialize the four inline E2E projects after the other 43 files passed; those four were run separately with the normal reporter. An earlier lease reached its two-hour lifetime during typechecking; the completed proof above uses the fresh lease.

Production: **+267/-203** (net +64); tests: **+124/-8** (net +116); docs: +5/-1. Production growth records the missing failure facts and reporting outcomes; the extracted importer is 232 lines and has one production caller.



Refs #156289 (second instance of the empty recovery report: zero moves, validation `not_run`, zero issues, while the real failure was a stale `databaseIdentity` receipt on the deferred plugin-session import blocking Gateway startup).
